previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted with fever, rigors, and right leg cellulitis. She had recently been treated for acute cellular rejection of her pancreas transplant and was on immunosuppressive therapy. Blood cultures identified E. coli bacteremia, and she was started on intravenous antibiotics and fluids for sepsis. Her condition improved with treatment, and a PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV vancomycin at home. Imaging showed stable transplanted organs with no signs of rejection or complications. She was discharged on oral ciprofloxacin, continued immunosuppression, and home nursing support, with plans to follow up with her nephrologist.

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
Ms. ___ is a ___ lady s/p kidney and pancreas transplants 
x2 in past, who came in for rigors at home without obvious 
source of infection.  She developed diarrhea and was C. diff 
positive, and after PO Flagyl she felt better so she was 
discharged home.
.
ACTIVE ISSUES:
.
# Rigors at home/Diarrhea here with Tmax 100.3: C. diff.
Upon admission, she was temporarily put on Vanc/Levo but these 
were stopped and she was doing fine for a few days. She had BKA 
stump pain but ruled out osteo with MRI and other infectious 
workup was negative. She developed diarrhea and C. diff positive 
(unclear if this accounts for her initial rigors at home b/c she 
had no loose stools at home, or if this was introduced in the 
hospital especially given that she received Levofloxacin). CMV 
VL is negative so this is an unlikely cause of her loose stools. 
 She was started on PO Flagyl with improvement in her symptoms 
and resolution of here diarrhea; she was afebrile.  Ms. ___ 
was discharged home on PO Flagyl 500 mg PO Q8H with plans to 
complete a 2 week course.  She will follow up with her 
Nephrologist and PCP.
.
# BKA stump pain: possibly neuropathic pain.
She developed extreme tenderness of her stump.  U/S was negative 
for clot or fluid collection. MRI ruled out osteo.  The pain was 
dull and there was tenderness; no electric shock feeling and no 
shooting pain.  Still, she was tried on uptitrated Gabapentin 
and she experienced relief.  She may have an element of 
neuropathic pain.  She will follow up with her PCP.
.
# Diabetes s/p Panc/Renal transplant: stable.
Her blood sugars were under good control, Cr close to baseline.  
Her Tacrolimus trough was elevated (~12.4) possibly from 
diarrhea.  It was temporarily held and returned to a goal range. 
 She was discharged on all the same immunosuppressants 
(Tacrolimus, Sirolimus, Prednisone).  She was continued on 
Acyclovir prophylaxis.  However, she was also started on monthly 
inhaled Pentamidine for PCP ___.
.
# HTN: labile blood pressures.
SBP ranged from 120-190.  She titrates her own medications at 
home.  She was continued on her home regimen and will follow up 
with her PCP.
.
INACTIVE ISSUES:
.
# Glaucoma/Dry eye: stable.
She was continued on Alphagan, Dorzolamide-Timolol, Restasis.
.
# Dyslipidemia: stable.
She was continued on Simvastatin, Omega 3 fatty acids, and ASA.
.
# Hypothyroidism: stable.
She was continued on Levothyroxine.
.
# Itching / Allergies: stable.
She was continued on hydroxizine prn.

INDICATION:  Question subcutaneous gas/osteomyelitis.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:  Diabetes type 1, status post left BKA, presents with
rigors at home.  Extreme left stump pain.

FINDINGS:  Atherosclerotic vascular calcifications.  No subcutaneous emphysema
identified.  No joint effusion.  No acute fractures.  No dislocation.  Mild
patellar enthesopathy.  

Status post BKA.  Heterotopic ossification is seen at the inferior stump of
the fibula.  Along the inferior aspect of the tibial stump, there is mild
periosteal reaction which may be due to infection. There is mild soft tissue
swelling subjacent to the stump.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Status post prior left BKA.
2.  Mild periosteal reaction along the distal stump of the tibia.  This may
represent a bone infection.  If further evaluation is needed, recommend MRI.

INDICATION:  Pain along the stump site in a patient with history of left
below-knee amputation.

COMPARISON:  MR from ___

FINDINGS:  Targeted sonography is performed in the region of reported pain,
specifically along the posteromedial aspect of the amputation stump site. 
There are no subjacent sonographic abnormalities, specifically no evidence of
subjacent fluid collection.

IMPRESSION:  No fluid collection identified in amputation stump site.

MRI OF THE CALF, ___

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Extreme left BKA stump pain, limiting the use of
prosthesis.  Query osteomyelitis.

COMPARISON:  Ultrasound and radiographs from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar non-contrast images of the left knee were acquired on
a 1.5 Tesla magnet per department protocol.

FINDINGS:  Comparison also made to previous calf MRI from ___. 
Since this previous study, edema in the subcutaneous tissues at the distal
aspect of the tibial stump has markedly decreased.  There is mild residual
edema in the medial subcutaneous tissues (4, 37).  However, increased T2
signal compatible with edema within the muscles around the tibia has
moderately increased, mainly in the medial gastrocnemius (4, 33).  There is a
small amount of high T2 signal, most probably representing fluid at the
myotendinous junction of the medial gastrocnemius (4, 29), and there is a
trace amount of more focal high signal just medial to the proximal tibia (4,
37), measuring 6 x 6 mm.

There is very faint increased signal at the distal aspect of the tibial stump
(6, 20), unchanged from previous exam.  This remains nonspecific and may be
reactive.  There is no definite evidence of osteomyelitis.  There is no new
marrow signal abnormality.

Generalized muscle atrophy is unchanged.  This study was not specifically
tailored for evaluation of internal derangements within the knee joint.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Unchanged minimal signal abnormality at the distal aspect of the tibial
stump is nonspecific, likely reactive.  No definite evidence of osteomyelitis
is seen.

2.  Marked decrease in subcutaneous edema about the distal aspect of the
tibial stump.

3.  Moderate increase in edema in the surrounding muscles, mainly the medial
gastrocnemius. Very small areas of fluid signal are seen at the myotendinous
junction of the medial gastrocnemius, and at the medial edge of the proximal
tibia as detailed above. This may represent an infective process, but no
drainable collection is identified.
